name: Vacuum-retention acceptance test of a vacuum-jacketed LN2 storage vessel: annulus evacuated to 50 microns or less, inner vessel filled and cooled with LN2, 48 h atmospheric hold then 1 h at MAWP (KSC-STD-Z-0009 Rev D 6.2.7)
plain_name: Fill a new vacuum-insulated liquid-nitrogen tank and check for two days that its insulating vacuum does not leak
description: The annular space of a double-walled cryogenic storage vessel is evacuated to 50 microns or less; the inner vessel and pipe are filled from the top and cooled to LN2 temperature while annulus pressure is logged; after stabilisation (5 degrees per hour or less) the vessel must hold atmospheric pressure for at least 48 h without annulus pressure rise or outer-shell condensation, then hold MAWP for at least 1 h.
keywords: Fill a new vacuum-insulated liquid-nitrogen tank and check for two days that its insulating vacuum does not leak

sources.citation: KSC-STD-Z-0009 Revision D, Design of Cryogenic Ground Systems and Ground Support Equipment, Standard for (NASA Kennedy Space Center)

requirements.rationale: The inner vessel is filled and cooled with liquid nitrogen.
The vacuum pumping system must bring the annular space to 50 microns (50 mTorr = 0.05 Torr) or less before the test continues.
The LN2-filled vessel must be held and monitored for at least 48 h.
